content:
After the launch of iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Duo this week, Apple has begun accepting trade-in credit for iPhone Air and iPhone 17. However, the iPhone Air trade-in deal is particularly disappointing this time, especially after the price hike this week.

Apple typically waits for new iPhone models to launch before accepting trade-ins, but that's not the case for the iPhone Air and iPhone 17 — there is still no iPhone Air 2 or iPhone 18, and the earliest we'd expect to see those new models is early next year.

However, Apple does want to give iPhone Air and iPhone 17 users the opportunity to upgrade to the iPhone 18 Pro or iPhone Duo, so these two models — still on sale but without newer versions — are eligible for trade-in.

Taking the iPhone 17 as an example, after this $100 price increase, the starting price is $899, and Apple offers a maximum trade-in credit of $585.

The iPhone Air also got a $100 price hike this week, bringing the starting price up to $1099. That's $200 more than the iPhone 17, but how much is the trade-in value? Also $585. It's painful to see.

Apple's trade-in value table almost looks like a pricing error, but Apple is most likely basing it on demand and component value — given that the iPhone Air uses nearly the same chip as the iPhone 17 Pro, this outcome is truly disappointing.

Overall, the iPhone Air has gained $100 in value for new customers, but its trade-in value — at least according to Apple's calculations — is the same as a model that's $200 cheaper. That's really not ideal.
